limitations: Every original position is retained. Measurements from failed positions are ineligible; no retry replaces a failure.
The source pin identifies this frozen cohort. Historical live process, socket, namespace and device audits are not rerun by extraction.
Pending path checks require succeeded, nominated exact owned UDP routes; resampling is bounded to 500 ms inside the original deadline. No stream behavior is changed.
Input quantiles use nearest rank on exact matched IDs. A ten-sample p95 is the sample maximum and supports no population-tail claim.
A 32x32 crop hash change is not whole-screen FPS; lossy noise can change it. Source-ID changes are separate. Canvas observation is not physical scanout.
Browser RTP, observer, controller, proxy, server CPU and browser CPU windows differ. UDP payload includes both directions and protocol traffic, excluding IP and link overhead.

CPU percentages and RSS are recorded summaries. Raw server ticks, clock rate, browser per-process CPU counters and their boundary samples are not retained, so these rates cannot be independently rederived.
Browser nackCount is the retained browser NACK counter. Server receivedNACKs is unavailable in this schema; it is not inferred from browser counts.
H.264 starts at 1 Mbps and VP8 at 500 kbps with REMB adaptation. Bitrates and image qualities are unequal.

The native comparison used different capture, encoding, bitrate, queueing and accounting. Its device environment lacks this browser mount proof. No matched-quality or native-performance claim is made here.
Deterministic userspace delay and periodic datagram loss are not an Internet path, random loss, a bandwidth cap or a capacity result.
Original v1/v2/v4 failures and original v5 smoke at five of six remain retained. V3 VM execution was zero; no v3 failures are invented. This extraction does not replace or promote earlier evidence.
